key_insight: A combinatorial vapor-deposition workflow independently tunes Cs/Pb and Br/Cl in wide-bandgap perovskites and identifies a Cs/Pb window of 1.05–1.20 plus a high-energy optical transition as key to higher photoluminescence yield.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable, data-driven route to optimize wide-bandgap perovskites for photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices without relying on slow, solution-only trial-and-error workflows.
method: Sequential physical vapor deposition for combinatorial composition control
Automated structural, compositional, and optical characterization
High-throughput screening across >500 sample regions in Cs-Pb-Br-Cl space
evidence_signal: The study reports screening more than 500 sample regions and links elevated PL yields to a defined compositional window and a robust optical signature.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a specific quaternary composition space, so transferability to other perovskite chemistries or device architectures may require revalidation.
paper_title: Tuning the optoelectronic properties of wide bandgap perovskites: Data-driven insights from combinatorial synthesis and high-throughput experimentation
